Exactly TWO female-read designs per sheet as specified, subtly lashes/styling, no human anatomy. Distinguish silhouettes/eyes/mouth/poses BEFOREprops. No automatic grins, repeated V-brows,O-mouth slot or bottom-right tongue.
READING ORDER left-right top-bottom:
1. INDIGNANT: Male-read broad box-rounded goo body, two short crest nubs, tiny faded ochre pajama collar. One hand pressed to chest in offended disbelief, other palm sharply up near shoulder. One eye enormous and other narrowing, eyebrows uneven not matching V, wide CLOSED buckled pout with no outside teeth. Outrage at a petty inconvenience, not armed soldier anger.

4. RESIGNED: Male-read wide drooping pear blob with low wilted central crest. Holds ONE empty little cloth shopping bag loosely at side, other ink palm turned up in a tiny exhausted shrug. White eyes half-open looking down toward camera, brows folded into lopsided weary arches, mouth CLOSED diagonal sigh-line. Whole body softens but remains upright at full cell size, not melted puddle or lying down.
5. EXHAUSTED: Female-read broad round blob with one small floppy crest, modest lashes, tiny faded blue sleep-mask pushed ABOVE brows and fully clear of eyes. One ink hand supports cheek while other hangs naturally close against body. One heavy lid barely open but white sclera/red iris/black pupil visible, other eye open a little more, OPEN sideways yawn with two upper teeth and no tongue gag. Upright, not asleep sitting/lying, no pillow or bed.

One hand grips a single small plain bread roll near belly, other lightly pinches his OWN mouth corner trying to suppress a snicker. Sideways white eyes sparkle, one brow raised in amused judgement, OPEN narrow tilted grin reveals two irregular upper teeth. Everyday petty delight rather than villain cackle; not same smile as other cells, no cup or pirate gear.
Make these ordinary residents emotionally visceral and expressive, offbeat relatable clay ink creatures. Humble props few and readable;the reaction is the identity. All image lettering absent; English names live only in metadata. Preserve rounded whole ink identity and craftsmanship.
